name: GC Design System
summary: The Government of Canada's bilingual (English/French) design system, built and maintained by the Canadian Digital Service; it provides framework-agnostic web components with React, Angular and Vue packages, design tokens, CSS shortcuts and Figma libraries for GC digital services.

license.name: MIT License
license.notes: License of the cds-snc/gcds-components code. @gcds-core/components, -react, -vue, tokens and css-shortcuts declare MIT on npm; @gcds-core/components-angular declares no license. Licensing of the documentation site content was not separately verified.

notes: Replacement for bmw-group-design-system (rejected: no public BMW Group design system found). Distinct verified system: the federal Government of Canada design system, not the provincial ontario-design-system already in the registry; the About page says a dedicated team at the Canadian Digital Service builds and maintains it with the Canada.ca Experience Office, and the site states it is independent of the Web Experience Toolkit (WET) and GCWeb. npm packages moved from the @cdssnc scope (deprecated, last 0.47.0 in Jan 2026) to @gcds-core; component packages release in lockstep (1.7.0, 2026-10-21) and latestVersion is @gcds-core/components. The Develop page offers React, Angular, Vue and 'Other' (static sites, CMS, etc.) install paths; the README names Stencil.js as the build tool. figmaUrl is the 'GC Design System library' community file linked from the official design setup page (a French library and a token library are also linked); figma.com itself was not fetched. Docs are bilingual (EN/FR).

name: Système de Design de l'État

organization.name: Service d'Information du Gouvernement (SIG), French Government

summary: The French State's design system (DSFR), developed and maintained by the Service d'Information du Gouvernement; it provides HTML, CSS and JavaScript components for public websites, distributed as the @gouvfr/dsfr npm package, and its use is restricted to French government sites.

license.name: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab), with DSFR terms of use
license.notes: LICENSE.md: code under Etalab 2.0, but use is governed by the DSFR terms of use (doc/legal/cgu.md): it must not be used by entities outside the French public administration and its replication outside .gouv.fr domains is limited; Marianne fonts and some assets have specific conditions. npm license field: etalab-2.0.

notes: Replacement for palantir-blueprint (duplicate of blueprint). Distinct verified system: the French State's design system; no existing entry covers it (other government entries are UK, US, NHS, Ontario, Helsinki). The official docs site www.systeme-de-design.gouv.fr (linked from the README as 'Voir la documentation officielle') answers automated requests with a Cloudflare challenge (403 'Just a moment...'), so it is NOT recorded; homepageUrl uses the official GouvernementFR/dsfr repo and docsUrl its README (installation via npm create @gouvfr/dsfr, structure, usage). Integrator: re-check https://www.systeme-de-design.gouv.fr/ from an unrestricted network and, if it loads, set homepageUrl/docsUrl to it. The README says the tool is developed, maintained and managed by the SIG; the SIG page on info.gouv.fr is also Cloudflare-blocked, so organization.websiteUrl is null. Installing requires accepting the terms of use. isOpenSource is null because the open licence is paired with use restrictions. figmaUrl null (no Figma link verified).

name: NL Design System

organization.name: ICTU (for the Dutch Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations)

summary: A shared design system for Dutch government organisations, run by a core team at ICTU for the Ministry of the Interior (BZK); components mature through Help Wanted, Community, Candidate and Hall of Fame stages, and core Candidate components ship as themeable CSS, React and token packages.

license.name: European Union Public Licence v1.2
license.notes: Copyleft licence of the nl-design-system/candidate repo; checked candidate packages declare EUPL-1.2 on npm. The site colofon states the project uses EUPL 1.2 and CC0 1.0 (the candidate README carries a CC0-1.0 header).

notes: Replacement for elastic-ui-framework (duplicate of elastic-ui). Distinct verified system: the Dutch government's shared system; the site calls it 'not an ordinary design system' but a collection of design systems (Utrecht, Den Haag, Amsterdam, Rotterdam, RVO, Rijkshuisstijl Community, etc.) working toward a Hall of Fame via the 'estafettemodel'. About page: carried out by ICTU on behalf of the Ministry of BZK. repositoryUrl is nl-design-system/candidate, which carries the core-team Candidate packages (components-css, components-react, tokens); packages are per component and versioned independently, so latestVersion and packageName are null (button/heading packages listed as examples). The developer handbook lists CSS, React, Web Component, Angular, Vue.js, HTML and Twig implementations; only CSS and React are in the Candidate repo, so web-components/angular/vue are recorded as community (Twig has no taxonomy slug). Brand themes use Design Tokens JSON. figmaUrl is the core-team 'NL Design System - Bibliotheek - Start' library linked from the official /figma/ page.

notes: Replacement for adobe-react-aria (duplicate of react-aria). Distinct verified system: Vercel's own product design system; not shadcn/ui (separate entry, a copy-paste component collection) and not Geist UI (geist-org/geist-ui, an unofficial community React library whose site now reads 'Archived - Geist UI'), which is not recorded. Documentation-only: the intro page describes Components as 'Building blocks for React applications', but ATLAS found no public package or repository for them, so frameworks is empty, repositoryUrl null and license null (no terms stated for the docs or components). The only distributed artifact is the Geist typeface (npm geist, SIL OFL 1.1 per vercel/geist-font OFL.txt), listed under packages; latestVersion is null because the font is versioned separately. Maintenance 'active' from sitemap lastmod for /geist/* pages (2026-10-31 to 2026-11-04, likely deploy timestamps), the 'Introducing Geist Serif' post (30 Oct 2026) and the font release. No Figma link found on the docs pages.
